mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility is declining monotonically (6.6→3.7% over four weeks), indicating people are spending less time at home and more time outside. This sustained outbound shift will drive retail-and-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks as the baseline activity level normalizes.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.6% to 3.7% over four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL stabilizes above 4% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has contracted sharply and consistently (−30.0% to −27.3%), signaling suppressed commuting. When transit recovery begins, retail-and-recreation mobility will rise within one week as commuters resume discretionary shopping and dining trips bundled with transit use.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at −27.3% in t-0w, up 3.7 points from t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days of a TRANSIT increase exceeding 3 percentage points, or TRANSIT remains below −25% for the entire forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has collapsed (−15.3% to −16.9%), indicating suppressed outdoor recreation. Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility remains stable (1.3–2.3%), showing essential trips are unaffected. The divergence signals a seasonal or weather-driven suppression of discretionary outdoor activity that will reverse, lifting retail-and-recreation as parks recover.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above −10% while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable within ±1 percentage point
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM divergence suggests selective suppression
failure_condition: PARKS does not recover above −10% within 14 days, or RETAIL_REC declines despite parks recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Workplaces mobility has improved steadily (−9.7% to −8.4% over four weeks), indicating gradual return to office routines. This trend will continue to drive retail-and-recreation upward as office workers resume weekday shopping and lunch-hour discretionary trips over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from −9.7% to −8.4% over four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not continue to improve or reverses by more than 1 percentage point, or RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation mobility has stabilized in a narrow band (−8.0% to −7.0%) despite volatility in other domains, indicating a floor effect. When transit and workplace mobility both improve simultaneously, retail will break upward as the suppressed demand is released through multiple activity channels.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by more than 1 percentage point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC range is only 1.0 percentage point over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days of simultaneous TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improvement, or both proxies fail to improve together.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility is near-zero (1.3%), indicating essential-trip suppression or saturation. If this remains constrained while parks and transit recover, retail-and-recreation will decline as consumers redirect discretionary spending toward outdoor and transit-adjacent activities rather than indoor retail.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0.5% while PARKS and TRANSIT both improve
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 1.3% suggests constrained essential-trip demand
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM recovers above 2% before PARKS and TRANSIT improve.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has shown extreme volatility (−15.3% to −27.3% to −16.9%), suggesting weather or seasonal shocks. If parks remain suppressed below −15% for the next two weeks, retail-and-recreation will decline as consumers avoid outdoor-adjacent retail (e.g., sports, recreation goods) and concentrate on essential shopping.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below −15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS volatility from −15.3% to −27.3% to −16.9% suggests external shock
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above −10% within 14 days, or RETAIL_REC rises despite sustained parks suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility decline (6.6%→3.7%) combined with stable grocery-and-pharmacy (1.3–2.3%) indicates people are leaving home but not for essential shopping. If this pattern persists and transit remains depressed below −25%, retail-and-recreation will fall as the outbound activity is directed toward non-retail venues (parks, workplaces) rather than retail centers.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4% and TRANSIT remains below −25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 3.7% with GROCERY_PHARM stable suggests non-retail outbound activity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, or TRANSIT recovers above −20% before RESIDENTIAL stabilizes.
